title: Code de la route vocabulary
_note: code-route-vocab run, 2026-11-12: French words written by hand for France, not yet checked by a second reader. Vocabulary only: no official exam questions and no text from any official source. translations.en = English meaning; deHint = German translation (the 'German' tab). Words already in the lexicon are refs; a ref's own en/deHint/example gives the driving sense. Instruction phrases are in the vous form an examiner uses; the example gives the tu form.
intro: Start with the group you need, from the parts of the car to what your instructor says. This deck is vocabulary only: it has no official exam questions, it doesn't replace a driving school or the official material, and it won't prepare you for the exam on its own.
introEasy: Do you want to drive in France? Learn the words for the car, the road, the exam and the papers here.
tipps: Learn both registers. Instructors and friends often say tu (Tourne à droite), examiners say vous (Tournez à droite). It means the same, so practise both forms.
Official papers use a formal word where people say another: the carte grise is officially the certificat d'immatriculation, and un PV is a procès-verbal. Learn both.
Say the instructions out loud while you sit in a parked car, or as a passenger. You will understand them faster once you are at the wheel.
